| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-001 | Maintainer Review — Comment Quality | Workflow ID: $WORKFLOW_ID | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-002 | Phase 1: LOAD | Default to writing no comments. | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-003 | Phase 1: LOAD | Only add when the WHY is nonobvious (hidden constraint, subtle invariant, workaround). | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-004 | Phase 1: LOAD | Don't explain WHAT (wellnamed identifiers do that). | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-005 | Phase 1: LOAD | Don't reference the current task / fix / callers ("used by X", "added for Y") — those rot. | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-006 | Phase 1: LOAD | Never write multiparagraph docstrings or multiline comment blocks unless absolutely necessary. | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-007 | Accuracy | Does the comment match what the code actually does? | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-008 | Accuracy | If the comment was modified to reflect a code change, does the rest of it still match? | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-009 | Value | Does the comment explain a nonobvious WHY (constraint, invariant, gotcha)? | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-010 | Value | Or does it restate WHAT the code does? (Restating WHAT = comment rot risk.) | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-011 | Value | Does it reference task IDs, callers, or PR numbers that will be meaningless in a year? | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-012 | Maintenance risk | Is the comment likely to drift out of date when the code changes? | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-013 | Maintenance risk | Is it tied to a specific implementation detail that might be refactored? | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-014 | Style | One short line preferred. Multiline blocks only when truly necessary. | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-015 | Style | No trailing summaries that just describe the next line. | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-016 | HIGH — inaccurate comments (don't match the code) | <file:line>: <description> | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-017 | HIGH — inaccurate comments (don't match the code) | Suggested fix: <update or remove> | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-018 | MEDIUM — comment rot risk | (same format — references that will rot, restatedwhatnotwhy, multiparagraph fluff) | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-019 | LOW — style / consistency | (same format) | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-020 | CHECKPOINT | `$ARTIFACTS_DIR/review/commentqualityfindings.md` written. | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-021 | CHECKPOINT | Each HIGH cites the exact comment text and the code it disagrees with. | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-COMMENT-QUALITY-022 | CHECKPOINT | Don't flag every short comment — many are intentionally brief. | maintainer-review-comment-quality.md |

| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-001 | Maintainer Review — Gate | Workflow ID: $WORKFLOW_ID | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-002 | Maintainer context (direction.md, profile.md, prior state, recent briefs, clock) | `direction` — the project's committed direction.md (what Archon IS / IS NOT, open questions) | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-003 | Maintainer context (direction.md, profile.md, prior state, recent briefs, clock) | `profile` — the running maintainer's profile.md (role, scope, current focus) | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-004 | Maintainer context (direction.md, profile.md, prior state, recent briefs, clock) | `prior_state` — last morningstandup state.json (carry_over may already mention this PR) | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-005 | Maintainer context (direction.md, profile.md, prior state, recent briefs, clock) | `recent_briefs` — last 3 daily briefs (look here if this PR was previously flagged) | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-006 | Maintainer context (direction.md, profile.md, prior state, recent briefs, clock) | `today` — today's local date as `YYYYMMDD` (deterministic, set by the gather script) | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-007 | Maintainer context (direction.md, profile.md, prior state, recent briefs, clock) | `deadline_3d` — today + 3 calendar days, `YYYYMMDD` (precomputed for the decline comment's reply window) | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-008 | Gate A — Direction alignment | aligned: PR clearly fits one of the "What Archon IS" clauses, or extends an existing pattern. | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-009 | Gate A — Direction alignment | conflict: PR clearly violates a "What Archon is NOT" clause. Cite the specific clause (e.g. `direction.md §singledevelopertool`). | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-010 | Gate A — Direction alignment | unclear: PR raises a question `direction.md` doesn't answer (touches an "Open question" or a new concern). Note it for later directiondoc evolution. | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-011 | Gate B — Scope focus | focused: PR has a single feature, single fix, or single coherent refactor. Size is fine — a 2000line PR can be focused if it's all one feature. | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-012 | Gate B — Scope focus | multiple_concerns: PR mixes 2+ unrelated changes (e.g. "fix the bug + add new feature + bump deps + reformat"). The right action is to ask the contributor to split it. | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-013 | Gate B — Scope focus | too_broad: One ostensiblycoherent change but with sprawling collateral edits across unrelated subsystems. Fixable by tighter scope, but currently too much to review. | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-014 | Gate B — Scope focus | Diff structure: do the changed files cluster around a single concern, or sprawl? | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-015 | Gate B — Scope focus | Title + body: does the contributor describe one change, or several "while I was here" changes? | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-016 | Gate B — Scope focus | Commit history if visible in `gh pr view`: is the PR a single coherent story, or accreted fixes? | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-017 | Gate C — Template quality | good: All template sections completed thoughtfully (Summary, Validation, Security, Rollback, etc.). | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-018 | Gate C — Template quality | partial: Template structure present but several sections empty or perfunctory ("N/A", "TBD", or singleword answers where prose is expected). | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-019 | Gate C — Template quality | empty: No template, or template skeleton with all sections blank. | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-020 | Tone rules | Open with thanks for the contribution. Always. | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-021 | Tone rules | Be specific about why — cite the direction.md clause, name the multiple concerns, list the empty template sections. Vague "this isn't a fit" is not acceptable. | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-022 | Tone rules | Offer a concrete path forward when one exists (split into PRs A + B + C; pick a different scope; fill in template sections X/Y/Z). | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-023 | Tone rules | Include a 3day reply window: state the date 3 days from today. If the contributor doesn't reply by then with reasoning to keep the PR open, it will be closed. Don't say "automatically" — the maintainer will close manually. | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-024 | Tone rules | No corporatespeak, no emoji, no AIattribution. | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-025 | Templates by category | For `decline` (direction conflict): | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-026 | Templates by category | For `needs_split` (multiple concerns): | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-027 | Templates by category | For `needs_split` (too broad / sprawling): | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-028 | Cited direction clauses | direction.md §<clause1> | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-029 | Cited direction clauses | direction.md §<clause2> | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-030 | Phase 6: RETURN STRUCTURED OUTPUT | This is the final step. After the artifacts are written, your entire response must be ONE JSON object — nothing else. | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-031 | Phase 6: RETURN STRUCTURED OUTPUT | NOT ALLOWED: | maintainer-review-gate.md |

| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-033 | Phase 6: RETURN STRUCTURED OUTPUT | Prose after the JSON ("This concludes the gate decision."). | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-034 | Phase 6: RETURN STRUCTURED OUTPUT | Bulletpoint summaries restating fields. | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-035 | Phase 6: RETURN STRUCTURED OUTPUT | Markdown headers like `Gate A`. | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-036 | Phase 6: RETURN STRUCTURED OUTPUT | Any text outside the single JSON object or its fences. | maintainer-review-gate.md |

| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-038 | Required fields | `direction_alignment`: `aligned` / `conflict` / `unclear` | maintainer-review-gate.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-REVIEW-GATE-039 | Required fields | `scope_assessment`: `focused` / `multiple_concerns` / `too_broad` | maintainer-review-gate.md |

| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-002 | Output format (read this FIRST, follow exactly) | Hard rules: | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-003 | Output format (read this FIRST, follow exactly) | Start the response with the `#` heading. No prose preamble. No "Looking at the data...", no `<thinking>`, no analysis dump, no "Now I'll synthesize...". | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-004 | Output format (read this FIRST, follow exactly) | Do NOT wrap the response in a JSON object. Specifically: do NOT output `{"brief_markdown": "...", "next_state": {...}}` — that is the OLD contract and is wrong. | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-005 | Output format (read this FIRST, follow exactly) | Do NOT use markdown code fences around the `ARCHON_STATE_JSON_BEGIN`/`ARCHON_STATE_JSON_END` markers — the markers must be plain lines. | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-006 | Output format (read this FIRST, follow exactly) | Nothing after the closing marker. The closing marker is the last line of your response. | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-007 | Output format (read this FIRST, follow exactly) | Skeleton example (illustrative — your actual brief uses real content): | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-008 | Since last run | ... | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-009 | P1 — Do today | PR #N — ... | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-010 | 2b. Compare prior state to current reality (progress detection) | Resolved since last run: PRs in `prior_state.observed_prs` whose numbers do NOT appear in current `ghdata.output.all_open_prs` — they were closed or merged. Crossreference against `ghdata.output.recently_closed_prs` to know whether they merged or were closed without merging. Same for issues. | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-011 | 2b. Compare prior state to current reality (progress detection) | Carryover revisited: each item in `prior_state.carry_over` — is it still open? Did its status change? If resolved, mention briefly under "Resolved since last run" and DROP from the state JSON's `carry_over`. If still pending, keep with original `first_seen` date (so age is preserved). | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-012 | 2b. Compare prior state to current reality (progress detection) | What you shipped: `ghdata.output.my_recent_commits` lists the maintainer's commits since the last run. Summarize meaningfully — group by area, highlight notable ones. Don't just list shas. | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-013 | 2b. Compare prior state to current reality (progress detection) | New since last run: PRs in current `all_open_prs` whose numbers are NOT in `prior_state.observed_prs` are new this run. Same for issues. | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-014 | 2c. Read the direction doc and profile | Profile scope drives breadth of coverage. `scope: everything` (main maintainer) means classify all open PRs, not just ones touching the maintainer's focus areas. | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-015 | 2c. Read the direction doc and profile | Direction clauses drive the politedecline classification. PRs adding multitenancy, hostedservice features, or anything contradicting the ISNOT list go to P4 with a citation. | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-016 | 2c. Read the direction doc and profile | Profile focus areas weight prioritization within P1P3 — items aligned with current focus rank higher. | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-017 | 2d. Triage all open PRs into P1-P4 | P1 (Do today): readytomerge PRs awaiting your review (`reviewDecision: APPROVED` or null AND `mergeStateStatus: clean`), security fixes, items breaking dev, blockers for an inflight release. Note: `mergeStateStatus` is the only CI/merge signal in the gathered payload (values: `clean`, `unstable`, `dirty`, `blocked`, `behind`, `unknown`). For ambiguous cases run `gh pr checks <number>` to verify CI before classifying as P1. | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-018 | 2d. Triage all open PRs into P1-P4 | P2 (This week): inflight PRs needing review or maintainer feedback, PRs with merge conflicts that can be unblocked, PRs from the maintainer's current focus areas that are progressing. | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-019 | 2d. Triage all open PRs into P1-P4 | P3 (Whenever): lowurgency items, drafts you authored, exploratory PRs, items outside current focus that aren't timesensitive. | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-020 | 2d. Triage all open PRs into P1-P4 | P4 (Politedecline candidates): PRs that conflict with `direction.md`. Each P4 entry MUST cite a specific clause (e.g., `direction.md §singledevelopertool`). | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-021 | 2h. Review-history awareness (cross-workflow memory) | Reviewed (review branch): `✓ reviewed Nd ago` — N is days between `readcontext.output.today` and `reviewed_at` (`YYYYMMDD` slice). Use `0d` for today, `1d` for yesterday, etc. | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-022 | 2h. Review-history awareness (cross-workflow memory) | Declined (decline / needs_split branch): `✓ declined Nd ago` — same age math, distinct verb so the brief reads correctly when a PR was politely declined rather than reviewed. | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-023 | 2h. Review-history awareness (cross-workflow memory) | Unclear: `✓ triaged Nd ago (unclear)` — for `gate_verdict: 'unclear'` runs. | maintainer-standup.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-024 | 2h. Review-history awareness (cross-workflow memory) | Staleness check: compare `reviewed_at` to the PR's `updatedAt` (in `ghdata.output.all_open_prs`). If `updatedAt > reviewed_at`, append `⚠ contributor pushed since` so the maintainer knows the prior review may need rerunning. Only flag when the gap is real and meaningful — sameday commits don't need a warning. | maintainer-standup.md |

## Extended Archon Governance (Sub-Folders)

| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-DIRECTION-001 | What Archon IS | A remote agentic coding platform. Control AI coding assistants (Claude Code SDK, Codex SDK, Pi community provider) remotely from Slack, Telegram, GitHub, Discord, CLI, and Web UI. | direction.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-DIRECTION-002 | What Archon IS | A singledeveloper tool. No multitenant complexity. Built for one practitioner running their own instance. | direction.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-DIRECTION-003 | What Archon IS | Platformagnostic at the conversation layer. Unified interface across adapters via `IPlatformAdapter`. Stream/batch AI responses in real time. | direction.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-DIRECTION-004 | What Archon IS | Workflowdriven. Reproducible AI execution chains defined as YAML DAGs in `.archon/workflows/`. Workflows run in isolated git worktrees by default. | direction.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-DIRECTION-005 | What Archon IS | Typesafe. Strict TypeScript everywhere. No `any` without justification. | direction.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-DIRECTION-006 | What Archon IS | Composable. Scripts in `.archon/scripts/`, commands in `.archon/commands/`, workflows compose them. | direction.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-DIRECTION-007 | What Archon IS | Selfhostable. Bun + TypeScript runtime. SQLite by default; PostgreSQL optional. Zero external service dependencies for core operation. | direction.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-DIRECTION-008 | What Archon is NOT | Not multitenant. No user accounts, role management, billing, or SaaS scaffolding. PRs adding these conflict with the singledeveloper thesis. | direction.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-DIRECTION-009 | What Archon is NOT | Not a hosted service. No proprietary backend dependencies. Selfhosted by design. | direction.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-DIRECTION-010 | What Archon is NOT | Not a generalpurpose chat UI. Adapters are conversation surfaces for workflow execution, not standalone chat experiences. | direction.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-DIRECTION-011 | What Archon is NOT | Not a replacement for the AI coding agent itself. Archon orchestrates Claude Code / Codex / Pi — it doesn't reimplement them. | direction.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-DIRECTION-012 | What Archon is NOT | Not opinionated about the dev environment. No mandatory editor integrations, framework lockin, or Docker requirement beyond what users opt into. | direction.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-DIRECTION-013 | What Archon is NOT | Not a workflow marketplace. Bundled workflows are reference patterns; Archon is not aiming to be a hub for thirdparty workflow distribution. | direction.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-DIRECTION-014 | Open questions (no stance yet) | (No open questions yet — populated over time.) | direction.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-DIRECTION-015 | How to evolve this doc | Add a "What Archon IS" or "is NOT" line when a PR triage forces a direction call. | direction.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-DIRECTION-016 | How to evolve this doc | Move "Open questions" entries to the IS / IS NOT sections once decided. | direction.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-DIRECTION-017 | How to evolve this doc | Reference the relevant clause in PR comments when declining: `direction.md §singledevelopertool`. | direction.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-DIRECTION-018 | How to evolve this doc | Keep entries short — one or two lines each. The point is fast lookup during triage, not a manifesto. | direction.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-README-001 | Setup for a new maintainer | Set `gh_handle` to your GitHub login. | README.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-README-002 | Setup for a new maintainer | Set `role` and `scope` to match your maintainer focus (`main_maintainer` / `everything` for full coverage; narrower for submaintainers). | README.md |

| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-README-004 | How it works (engine view) | `maintainerstandupgitstatus.ts` — fetches `origin/dev`, fastforwards if safe, captures new commits + diff stat since the last recorded SHA. | README.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-README-005 | How it works (engine view) | `maintainerstandupghdata.ts` — pulls open PRs (full metadata), reviewrequested PRs, authoredbyme PRs, assigned issues, recentlyfiled unlabeled issues, and recentlyclosed PRs/issues since the last run. | README.md |
| G-ARCHON-MAINTAINER-STANDUP-README-006 | How it works (engine view) | `maintainerstandupreadcontext.ts` — reads `direction.md`, `profile.md`, `state.json`, and the last 3 briefs. | README.md |

| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART1-GUIDE-011 | Key Talking Points | "Start with 35 teammates and 56 tasks per teammate for best results." | part1-guide.md |
| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART1-GUIDE-012 | Key Talking Points | "Nicholas Carlini ran 16 agents simultaneously  2,000 sessions, $20k in API costs  built a 100kline Rust C compiler that compiles the Linux kernel on x86, ARM, and RISCV. Passes 99% of GCC torture tests." | part1-guide.md |

| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART1-GUIDE-015 | Gotchas | Token costs are 24x a single session | part1-guide.md |
| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART1-GUIDE-016 | Gotchas | tmux required for split pane mode (VS Code terminal not supported) | part1-guide.md |

| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART2-GUIDE-020 | Key Talking Points | "Hooks in skill frontmatter are scoped — they only live while the skill runs. No global side effects." | part2-guide.md |
| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART2-GUIDE-021 | Key Talking Points | "The prompt hook is an LLM checking another LLM's work. That's the quality gate pattern — costs pennies, catches real mistakes." | part2-guide.md |
| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART2-GUIDE-022 | Key Talking Points | "`once: true` prevents the hook from firing repeatedly — useful for onetime setup or logging." | part2-guide.md |
| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART2-GUIDE-023 | Key Talking Points | "Dynamic context injection means Claude starts with real data, not instructions to go find it." | part2-guide.md |
| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART2-GUIDE-024 | Key Talking Points | "This skill uses both hook lifetimes: skillscoped during execution, settingslevel across sessions." | part2-guide.md |

| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART2-GUIDE-035 | Key Talking Points | "Skills define what to do. Agents define how to do it. Separating them makes both composable." | part2-guide.md |

| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART2-GUIDE-037 | Key Talking Points | "Context forking is information hygiene — 50K tokens of issue data stays in the fork." | part2-guide.md |
| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART2-GUIDE-038 | Key Talking Points | "The prompt hook catches incomplete label applications before they reach GitHub. Costs pennies per check." | part2-guide.md |

| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART2-GUIDE-052 | Key Talking Points | "14 features in one skill. Each is simple — the power is in composition." | part2-guide.md |
| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART2-GUIDE-053 | Key Talking Points | "The safety hook is a shell script. Reads JSON, checks a blocklist, exits 2 to block. No framework." | part2-guide.md |
| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART2-GUIDE-054 | Key Talking Points | "Memory makes the agent better over time. Each run builds on the last — it remembers the backlog." | part2-guide.md |
| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART2-GUIDE-055 | Key Talking Points | "The metajudge is an LLM evaluating another LLM. It writes structured feedback the agent reads next run." | part2-guide.md |
| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART2-GUIDE-056 | Key Talking Points | "Worktree isolation means the agent can break things safely. Your working directory is untouched." | part2-guide.md |
| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART2-GUIDE-057 | Key Talking Points | "The Slack notification uses a `SubagentStop` hook with a `matcher` — it only fires when the rulecheck agent finishes, not for every subagent. That's how you scope settingslevel hooks to specific agents." | part2-guide.md |
| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART2-GUIDE-058 | Key Talking Points | "The old rulecheck was advisory. This one actually fixes things. Same domain, fundamentally different capability." | part2-guide.md |
| G-ARCHON-WORKSHOP-PART2-GUIDE-059 | Key Talking Point | "The agent remembers what it fixed, what's left to fix, and what the metajudge said. Next run, it picks up where it left off." | part2-guide.md |

| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-057 | Recovery: deterministic release CI failure | Do not rerun the release workflow a third time hoping it succeeds. If the failure was reproducible twice, it's a code bug — you need to ship code to fix it. | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-058 | Diagnose | Bundler/bytecode bug — Bun `bytecode` produces invalid output for the current module graph. Symptom: `TypeError: Expected CommonJS module to have a function wrapper` at binary startup. Historically caused by a new dependency's CJS/ESM shape interacting with `bytecode` — dropping the flag or lazyimporting the offending module has been the fix. | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-059 | Diagnose | Moduleinit crash — a dependency does `readFileSync('package.json')` or similar at module top level via a path that exists in `node_modules/` but not next to a compiled binary. Symptom: every binary subcommand crashes immediately; error typically mentions a missing file adjacent to `process.execPath`. Fix by lazyimporting the dependency behind the code path that actually uses it. | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-060 | Diagnose | Smoketest timeout on Windows — not actually a bug in the code; the Windows runner is slow. Rerun once; if it recurs, bump the test timeout. | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-061 | Fix and re-release as the NEXT patch | Do not reuse `vx.y.z`. Cut `vx.y.(z+1)` (or nextminor if warranted) with the fix. Rationale: | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-062 | Fix and re-release as the NEXT patch | Tag immutability: `vx.y.z` is already recorded in git history and release cache | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-063 | Fix and re-release as the NEXT patch | Semver clarity: users and tooling should see a new version number when the bits change | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-064 | Fix and re-release as the NEXT patch | Audit trail: "v0.3.7 was cut but had no shipped binaries; v0.3.8 is the first release with <fix>" is cleaner than rewriting v0.3.7 | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-065 | Fixed | First release with working compiled binaries after vx.y.z's <bug>. vx.y.z was tagged but its binary smoke test failed deterministically (see RUN_ID in CI history). The tag is preserved for history; this release (vx.y.(z+1)) is the first with shipped binaries. `install.sh` and Homebrew were never updated to vx.y.z, so users were not exposed to the broken state. | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-066 | What NOT to do | Do not forcepush or rewrite the tag. Once a tag exists, it's a public promise of that SHA. Deleting and recreating to a different SHA is tagspoofing and breaks any downstream that cached the original. | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-067 | What NOT to do | Do not skip this recovery path to "just push more binaries to the broken release". The release exists with a specific commit SHA; uploading binaries built from a newer SHA creates binary/source drift that is hard to diagnose later. | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-068 | What NOT to do | Do not update the Homebrew formula before v0.3.(z+1) is fully shipped. The formula should always point at a version with all 7 assets uploaded and `/testrelease brew` passing. | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-069 | Important Rules | NEVER force push | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-070 | Important Rules | NEVER skip Step 1.5 (preflight compiledbinary smoke). If the stack is a Bun/Node project with a buildbinaries script, the `bun build compile` smoke test runs before version bump, PR, or tag. Skipping it means every bundler regression or moduleinit crash only surfaces after the tag is pushed — by which point `releases/latest` is already 404ing for every user. The ~30s cost is paid to keep the failure mode local. | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-071 | Important Rules | If Step 1.5 fails, abort the release and fix the underlying issue on a feature branch. Do not "just skip it" and hope CI doesn't repro the problem. | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-072 | Important Rules | NEVER skip the review step — always show the changelog before committing | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-073 | Important Rules | NEVER include "CoAuthoredBy: Claude" or any AI attribution in the commit | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-074 | Important Rules | NEVER add emoji to changelog entries unless the user asks | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-075 | Important Rules | If the user says "ship it" without specifying bump type, default to patch | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-076 | Important Rules | The commit message is just `Release x.y.z` — clean and simple | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-077 | Important Rules | NEVER update `homebrew/archon.rb` version field without also updating the `sha256` values. They must move together atomically. The correct SHAs only exist after the release workflow finishes building binaries — see Step 10. Updating the version field alone produces a stale formula that looks valid but causes checksum mismatches on install. | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-078 | Important Rules | NEVER skip Step 11 (tap sync). The `coleam00/Archon/homebrew/archon.rb` file is only a template; users install from `coleam00/homebrewarchon/Formula/archon.rb`. If you update one without the other, users get stale or wrong data. | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RELEASE-SKILL-079 | Important Rules | NEVER announce a release that failed `/testrelease brew`. A release that installs but crashes on first invocation is worse than no release — it burns user trust. If the release verification fails, cut a hotfix before telling anyone the release exists. | SKILL.md |

| G-ARCHON-RULECHECK-RULES-GUIDE-011 | Tier 3 — Medium (fix if time permits) | Nested ternaries — should be if/else or switch | rules-guide.md |
| G-ARCHON-RULECHECK-RULES-GUIDE-012 | Tier 3 — Medium (fix if time permits) | Clever code — metaprogramming or hidden dynamic behavior that obscures intent | rules-guide.md |

| G-ARCHON-RULECHECK-RULES-GUIDE-016 | Tier 4 — Low (note for backlog) | Comment quality — obvious comments, outdated descriptions | rules-guide.md |

| G-ARCHON-RULECHECK-SKILL-002 | Rules for You | Do NOT grep, read source files, or run linters — the agent handles all of that | SKILL.md |

| G-ARCHON-RULECHECK-SKILL-006 | Rules for You | Do NOT update project memory — the agent maintains its own memory at `.claude/agentmemory/rulecheckagent/`. Do not duplicate run results into your project memory. | SKILL.md |
| G-ARCHON-RULECHECK-SKILL-007 | Rules for You | Trust the agent. It runs in an isolated worktree and will create a PR when done. | SKILL.md |

| G-ARCHON-REFERENCES-REPO-INIT-002 | Directory Structure | `commands/` — Reusable prompt templates used by `command:` workflow nodes. Committed to git. | repo-init.md |
| G-ARCHON-REFERENCES-REPO-INIT-003 | Directory Structure | `workflows/` — YAML workflow definitions. Committed to git. | repo-init.md |
| G-ARCHON-REFERENCES-REPO-INIT-004 | Directory Structure | `scripts/` — Named TypeScript/JavaScript (bun) or Python (uv) scripts referenced by `script:` nodes. Extension determines runtime: `.ts`/`.js` → bun, `.py` → uv. Committed to git. | repo-init.md |
| G-ARCHON-REFERENCES-REPO-INIT-005 | Directory Structure | `mcp/` — MCP server JSON configs. Usually checked in with `$ENV_VAR` references; avoid hardcoding secrets. Some teams gitignore this and rely entirely on env expansion. | repo-init.md |
| G-ARCHON-REFERENCES-REPO-INIT-006 | Directory Structure | `state/` — Workflowwritten crossrun state (e.g. the `repotriage` dedup log). Always gitignore — these are runtime artifacts, not source. | repo-init.md |
| G-ARCHON-REFERENCES-REPO-INIT-007 | Directory Structure | `config.yaml` — Repospecific defaults (assistant, worktree settings, etc.). Committed to git. | repo-init.md |
| G-ARCHON-REFERENCES-REPO-INIT-008 | Directory Structure | `.env` — Reposcoped Archon env (loaded with `override: true` at boot). Do NOT commit. This is different from the target repo's toplevel `.env` — that file belongs to the target project, and Archon strips its autoloaded keys from subprocess env before spawning AI to prevent leakage. See ThreePath Env Model below. | repo-init.md |
| G-ARCHON-REFERENCES-REPO-INIT-009 | Worktree settings | .env.local | repo-init.md |

| G-ARCHON-REFERENCES-REPO-INIT-012 | How Bundled Defaults Work | To disable defaults: Set `defaults.loadDefaultWorkflows: false` or `defaults.loadDefaultCommands: false` in config. | repo-init.md |

| G-ARCHON-REFERENCES-REPO-INIT-015 | Three-Path Env Model | Targetproject env that a workflow needs (`GH_TOKEN`, `DOTENV_PRIVATE_KEY`, etc.) → see [PerProject Env Injection](#perprojectenvinjection) below. | repo-init.md |
| G-ARCHON-REFERENCES-REPO-INIT-016 | Three-Path Env Model | Targetproject env that Archon should NOT touch → leave it in `<cwd>/.env` where the project already expects it. Archon strips it from subprocess env but doesn't delete the file. | repo-init.md |
| G-ARCHON-REFERENCES-REPO-INIT-017 | Per-Project Env Injection | Option 1: `.archon/config.yaml` `env:` block (checked into git; values can be `$REF_NAME` expansions from Archon env): | repo-init.md |
| G-ARCHON-REFERENCES-REPO-INIT-018 | Per-Project Env Injection | Option 2: Web UI Settings → Projects → Env Vars — percodebase, stored in the Archon DB, values never returned over the API (only keys are listed). Use this for values that should NOT appear in git. | repo-init.md |

The `fs/promises` module is globally mocked by `githubcontext.test.ts`, causing `readFile` to return an empty string instead of actual package.json content. | issue-252-378.md |
| G-ARCHON-ISSUES-ISSUE-252-378-005 | Problem Statement | Issue #252: The test suite was reported to hang after completion due to `mock.module('../db/connection')` in `executor.test.ts`. This no longer reproduces on the current codebase (full suite completes in ~40s), likely due to the `commitAllChanges` spy that prevents `sendCriticalMessage` retry delays. Preventive cleanup should still be added. | issue-252-378.md |
